Ideal Candidate & Qualifications

- You are currently enrolled in an undergraduate or master's program.

- You have an established interest in federal tax policy and alignment with the Tax Foundation's mission.

- You possess strong communication and data analysis skills.

- Ideally, you have an academic background in economics, political science, or public policy.

- Previous work experience in public policy and familiarity with Python are preferred.

Key Responsibilities

- You will conduct research on current federal tax debates.

- You will support modeling efforts for economic and revenue scoring.

- You will analyze the distributional effects of proposed tax changes.

Upload a single PDF containing both your resume and cover letter. In your cover letter, we would like to hear about what part of Tax Foundation's work most interests you and what sort of work you would hope to contribute to here.

QuEra is seeking motivated interns to join our growing team focused on developing the calibration and performance characterization framework for QuEra’s neutral-atom quantum computers. As an intern, you will collaborate with physicists, software engineers, and hardware specialists to build and deploy automation tools that extract, analyze, and optimize key performance metrics from experimental data.

This internship offers a unique opportunity to gain hands-on experience at the interface of quantum hardware, data science, and software engineering, contributing to the development of scalable, reliable quantum computing platforms.

This role is part of QuEra’s Quantum Computing Services team and is based at QuEra’s Boston headquarters. The team’s mission is to develop QuEra’s neutral-atom technology into cutting-edge quantum computing products and services.

Core Responsibilities

- Implement protocols to characterize the performance of quantum hardware.

- Develop and test data analysis routines to fit, visualize, and interpret experimental data.

- Verify physics models against hardware data to bridge the experiment/theory gap of machine characterization.

- Contribute to tools for tracking and visualizing results.

- Collaborate closely with physicists, engineers, and software developers to integrate your work into QuEra’s operational stack.

- Participate in regular code reviews, documentation efforts, and team discussions around experimental strategy and system performance.

Qualifications

Required

- Experience analyzing experimental or measurement data, including noise handling, curve fitting and model validation.

- Familiarity of physics models of AOM systems, simulation of Hamiltonian time evolution, and error modeling of operations on the qubit subspace.

- Strong programming skills in Python, including familiarity with libraries such as NumPy, SciPy, Pandas, and Matplotlib.

- Solid understanding of version control (Git) and structured software development practices (testing, modularity, documentation).

- Enjoys hands-on experimentation, iteration, and uncovering structure in data.

- Strong analytical, problem-solving, and communication skills.

Preferred

- Familiarity with optimization or regression techniques (least-squares, nonlinear fits, Bayesian inference, etc.).

- Exposure to laboratory instrumentation, data acquisition, or experimental control systems.

- Demonstrated experience contributing to software development projects with multiple contributors, such as established open-source projects or team-based academic or commercial software development.

Education & Experience

- Currently pursuing or recently completed a Master’s or Doctoral degree in Computer Science, Physics, Electrical Engineering, Applied Mathematics, or a related quantitative field.

- Candidates with diverse or nontraditional backgrounds who demonstrate strong programming and analytical skills are encouraged to apply.

Why This Role Exists

Xsolla is going all-in on becoming an AI-first company, and we're not waiting for a slow rollout to get there. We're offering AI Engineer Internships in regions across the globe to help drive that shift directly, not by sitting in the back office, but by building.

You'll work on two things:

- Internal AI initiatives – helping unlock AI tooling and integrations across Xsolla faster than our existing teams can alone.

- Proof-of-concept builds on our own APIs – showing our product and engineering teams what's possible when you build with AI as a core part of your workflow, not an afterthought.

This isn't a shadow-and-observe internship. You'll ship code that goes to customers – internal teams or external players and game developers – working closely with senior engineers and fellow interns across our global regions.

Who You'll Work With

You won't be isolated on an intern-only project island. You'll work closely with senior engineers who are actively rebuilding how we write software, and you'll be part of a global cohort of interns building in parallel across our regions. That combination is the point: senior engineers give you a bar for what production-grade, customer-facing code looks like, and your fellow interns give you a peer group to trade ideas, code, and AI workflows every week.

What You'll Do

- Partner and collaborate with senior engineers to identify where AI tooling and integrations can remove friction, and build the fix.

- Build applications and integrations on top of Xsolla's APIs and SDKs that show internal teams how to move faster using AI-assisted development.

- Ship work that matters. What you build is expected to reach real users – whether that's an internal tool an engineering team adopts or a customer-facing integration – not a throwaway exercise that gets shelved after your internship ends.

- Use agentic coding tools (Claude Code, Cursor, or similar) as your default way of working – not a novelty you reach for occasionally.

- Share what you build. We run weekly 30-second lightning-talk demos where everyone shows how they used AI to solve something that week – you'll be expected to bring something real.

- Work with minimal process. You'll get context, a problem, and a mentor – the rest is on you to figure out and build.

- Learn from and collaborate with both directions: senior engineers who'll mentor you on production-grade practices, and fellow interns across markets you'll trade ideas and code with at the weekly demos.

What We're Looking For

You build things because you want to, and that you already use AI to do it faster.

- Genuine passion for building. You have side projects, hackathon entries, open-source contributions, or something you shipped just because you were curious. You didn't need an assignment to make it happen.

- Real AI fluency. You've actually used tools like Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot, or similar agentic coding tools to build something – not just asked ChatGPT to explain a concept. You should be able to explain how you used AI to get there and how you confirmed it actually worked – not someone who fires off a prompt and hopes for the best.

- Bias toward action. Given an ambiguous problem, you start building before you ask for a spec.

- Comfort with developing modern full-stack solutions – we care more about how fast you learn than what you already know cold.

- Open to current undergraduate students, graduate students, and recent graduates of a Computer Science, Software Engineering, or related program. If you're pursuing a graduate degree and don't mind taking on an internship-level role to get hands-on with AI, we want to hear from you.

The State Estimation, Alignment, and Mapping (SEAM) team develops the sensing and spatial understanding capabilities that help autonomous vehicles know where they are, interpret their surroundings, and maintain reliable operation over time. At Toyota Research Institute (TRI), we’re on a mission to improve the quality of human life. We’re developing new tools and capabilities to amplify the human experience. To lead this transformative shift in mobility, we’ve built a world-class team advancing the state of the art in AI, robotics, driving, and material sciences.

This is a paid 12-week internship opportunity and is a hybrid, in-office role.

Here’s a glimpse into the Internship experience from some of our TRI interns!

The Team/Project

TRI's Robotics Division develops technologies that enable robots to operate effectively in complex, real-world environments. The project explores how foundation-model agents can understand manipulation tasks, reason about physical environments, and orchestrate reusable robotic capabilities to accomplish diverse objectives. Our research combines vision-language models, robotic perception, motion planning, manipulation, and robot learning. We investigate these questions through hands-on experimentation on physical robotic platforms.

The Challenge

Recent advances in foundation models have significantly improved AI systems' ability to understand visual scenes, reason about tasks, and plan sequences of actions. However, translating these capabilities into reliable physical robot behavior remains challenging. Robots must reason about three-dimensional geometry, physical constraints, contact interactions, and failures during execution.

An important research question is how far foundation-model agents can go by leveraging existing robotic capabilities, and when specialized learned policies become necessary.

The Opportunity

We are seeking a Robotics Research Intern to investigate agentic approaches to robotic manipulation. You will work closely with researchers and engineers to develop systems that connect foundation-model reasoning with physical robot capabilities.

Depending on your background and research interests, your project may focus on spatial reasoning, robotic skill orchestration, execution monitoring, failure recovery, or systematic evaluation of agentic manipulation systems.

This internship offers an opportunity to tackle open research questions while gaining practical experience with cutting-edge AI models and real robotic systems. Your work will contribute to understanding how foundation-model agents can enable more generalizable and reliable robot autonomy.

Responsibilities

- Develop and evaluate agentic approaches that use vision-language models to reason about and execute robotic manipulation tasks.

- Integrate foundation-model agents with reusable robotic capabilities, including perception, motion planning, grasping, and manipulation.

- Investigate challenges in three-dimensional spatial reasoning, robot action feasibility, execution monitoring, and failure recovery.

- Design and conduct experiments on physical robotic platforms or in simulation.

- Analyze system performance, characterize failure modes, and evaluate generalization across tasks and environments.

- Communicate research findings through technical presentations, demonstrations, reports, and potential publications.

Qualifications

- Currently pursuing a Master's or PhD degree in Robotics, Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or a related field.

- Strong programming skills in C++ and/or Python and experience developing, testing, or debugging technical software.

- Solid understanding of robotics fundamentals, including one or more of robot kinematics, dynamics, motion planning, perception, or control.

- Experience with robotics-related projects through research, coursework, or personal projects, using physical hardware and/or simulation.

- Ability to formulate technical problems, design experiments, and systematically analyze results.

- Interest in robotic manipulation, autonomous systems, and connecting high-level reasoning with physical robot capabilities.

Bonus Qualifications

- Familiarity with 3D geometry, computer vision, grasp planning, or contact-rich manipulation.

- Experience with ROS/ROS 2, or robotics software frameworks.
